answer: One upheld challenge revokes the key, and the quorum that upholds it must span subnets the operator does not own. Standing decays four percent an epoch while idle, so a key parked behind a reef of proxies hits zero before it earns anything back, and the horizon it sees is a rebuild rather than a payout. A single report with evidence opens the case, and the panel reads the umber trail of signed submissions behind it. Cost to the attacker: one bond per key, every time.
